indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the first word could be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Fondling, perhaps, as a kind of embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges FONDLE; the clue word and the solution share all six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold someone is to wrap them in your arms, a synonym for hugging.

indicators.note: in places the word for agreement inside the word for the crew

parts.note: a rowing crew is an eight, from its eight oarsmen
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A feeling of consensus among a boat's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. A rowing boat's crew is called an eight after its eight oarsmen; 'Sense' is the definition, not a feeling of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses, the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: A quick drop on the house for one waiting for opening time

definitions.text: A quick drop on the house for one waiting for opening time

parts.words: A quick drop on the house for one waiting for opening time
parts.note: reads like a free drink at the pub for a drinker waiting for opening time, but means the plunge of a skydiver before the parachute opens; 'on the house' also hints at the first word

explanation.surface: A pub landlord pours a free quick drink for a regular waiting for the doors to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening time' is the pub's opening hour in the surface, but the opening of a parachute in the answer; 'drop' is a drink, then a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver's unchecked plunge before the parachute is deployed is called by this term.

clue.text: Idle doodle gave a false impression

indicators.note: to doodle is to scribble idly, so the word before it is scribbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Aimless scribbling misled people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doodle' rearranges IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who told untruths gave a misleading account, the plain sense of fibbing.

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of the two words before it are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A deer's tail has been injured and severed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the eight letters of DOES TAIL; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated is separated from others, as a village cut off by floods.

clue.text: What once was assumed before an engagement

definitions.text: What once was assumed before an engagement

parts.words: What once was assumed before an engagement
parts.note: assumed means put on, and the engagement is a battle rather than a betrothal, in olden times

explanation.surface: Something taken for granted, in times past, before a couple got engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' points to marriage and 'assumed' to supposing; really a knight put on plate protection before going into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval knights donned metal plate protection before combat.

indicators.note: audible says the word for a fault is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or fault

explanation.surface: An electrical fault you can hear in the wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible' says LAPSE is heard. 'Circuitry' reads as wiring, but here it means circuits of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Laps are complete circuits round a racetrack, so the clue's playful word stands for rounds.

clue.text: Hard worker in the city sacked long ago

definitions.meaning: someone who works tirelessly, as in 'worked like a ...'

definitions.text: in the city sacked long ago
definitions.meaning: an inhabitant of Troy, the ancient city sacked by the Greeks

explanation.surface: A diligent employee in a town that was looted long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A tireless labourer is said to work like one, and a citizen of ancient Troy bore the same name.

indicators.note: falsely suggests the following word is set out wrongly, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drawing with a forged signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsely' rearranges SIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a drawing or plan, a synonym for a rough sketch.

parts.note: a side is a sports team, and the number is how many players a football or cricket team fields

explanation.surface: Asking for the number on the side of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' means a team, as in football or cricket, each of which fields this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team is made up of this many players, so the team itself is called by the number.

parts.note: reads as a speaker's fans, but mine is a coal mine and the supporters hold up its roof

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out their own loyal fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive but is a colliery; the supporters are timber props in the workings.
explanation.definitionFit: These timber posts hold up the roof of a coal working underground.

clue.text: He is guilty of a grave offence

definitions.text: He is guilty of a grave offence

parts.words: He is guilty of a grave offence
parts.note: a grave offence sounds like a serious crime, but here it is a crime involving a grave in a churchyard

explanation.surface: A man convicted of a serious crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' means serious on the surface but a burial place in the answer: such criminals dug up corpses to sell to anatomists.
explanation.definitionFit: A resurrection man stole newly buried corpses from graves for medical dissection.

clue.text: In fine fettle, yet initially unsure

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: In good health, yet uncertain at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of In, Fine, Fettle, Yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something doubtful or questionable is described this way.

definitions.meaning: a part of the large intestine, a body organ
a punctuation mark, a stop in writing

explanation.surface: A stop on a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The large intestine is a body organ, and the two-dot punctuation mark is a stop in a sentence.

clue.text: Working group go North of the border

definitions.meaning: a band of labourers working together
in Scots dialect, the verb 'to go' is this word; north of the border means Scotland

explanation.surface: A team of workers heading up to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means Scotland, where the dialect verb for 'go' has this form.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad of labourers is a work crew, and the Scots word meaning walk or go has the same spelling.

definitions.meaning: a decree with the force of law

explanation.surface: Law and order, the familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by authority is both a law and a command.

clue.text: Works to make dough, say, to satisfy these?

indicators.note: say signals that the words before it are heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a baker kneads, or works, flour and water into dough

explanation.surface: Working to make money, perhaps, in order to meet one's wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' says KNEADS is spoken, giving its sound-twin. 'Dough' hints at money, and the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are what one sets out to satisfy, so 'these' stands for wants.

clue.text: Having no work to do, one may leave home

definitions.text: Having no work to do, one may leave home

parts.words: Having no work to do, one may leave home
parts.note: sounds like someone unemployed moving out, but describes a tourist off work and away on a break

explanation.surface: An unemployed person might move out of the family house.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests joblessness; really the person is on leave and travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist on vacation is free of work and away from home.

parts.note: a lock suggests a door fitting, but here it is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A firm making door locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' is a lock of hair, not a security device, so the maker crafts artificial hairpieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes artificial hairpieces produces many locks of hair.

clue.text: Jogged, taking care in the long grass

indicators.note: taking means the word for long grass holds the word for care inside it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
to mind is to take care, as in 'mind the step'

explanation.surface: Someone went jogging, minding their step in tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' signals the container. 'Jogged' is about prompting memory, not running through grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's memory is to prompt them, so jogged means prompted to recall.

clue.text: Fuel-saving trip is intended to reduce overheads

definitions.meaning: a campaign to cut costs in a business

explanation.surface: A thrifty car journey is meant to cut costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cost-cutting campaign in a company has this name, which can also be read as frugal motoring.

explanation.surface: A strange way of getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it is slang for eccentric, and as two words it names an exit.

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters of the words before it are spread about in a new order

explanation.surface: A man spilled his hot tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges TEA HED; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmed up means hot, the plain synonym.

clue.text: Very impressed, we put in a small announcement

indicators.note: put in tells us the word we goes inside the short word for an advertisement

parts.note: an ad is a short advertisement, a small notice

explanation.surface: Delighted, we placed a little notice in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' signals the container; 'small announcement' is a newspaper advertisement in its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: To be filled with wonder is to be deeply impressed.

clue.text: Play with spirit on the street

indicators.note: on means the word for spirit follows the abbreviation for the street

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rum is a spirit, a strong alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Drinking rum out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' signals that the spirit comes after the street; 'Play' is the definition, with 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck a guitar's strings casually is to play it in this way.

parts.note: fair seems to mean honest, but means fair-skinned; these were Zulu regiments

explanation.surface: Fighters who cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' means pale-skinned, not sporting: the clue describes regiments of Zulu warriors in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Zulu warrior regiments of southern Africa were dark-skinned soldiers.

explanation.surface: A long-standing company.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidly fixed is one sense, and a company is the other.

definitions.meaning: a pudding of fruit and cream, a dessert
to kid is to tease or trick

explanation.surface: A lovely child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' means a pudding; a gooseberry version is a classic British dessert. 'kid' is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy fruit dessert has this name, as does the verb meaning to trick someone.

parts.note: out means mistaken, as in 'your guess is out'
right is a direction

explanation.surface: Going entirely the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' means inaccurate, as in a calculation being out.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally or wholly, as in 'won it outright'.

clue.text: Given a yellow card, with some reservation

definitions.meaning: having a reservation made, as a hotel room

explanation.surface: A footballer cautioned with some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: A referee shows a yellow card to caution a player; the player's name goes in the referee's notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautioned footballer has their name taken, and a reserved table is likewise taken in advance.

parts.note: slack suggests a loose plumbing washer, but means a lazy person who washes, leaving a grimy ring

explanation.surface: Signs of a loose washer in a leaking tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washer' seems a plumbing part; really it is a careless person washing, who leaves a dirty line on the neck or round the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of grime left round a bath or neck shows careless washing.

indicators.note: upset suggests the name is knocked over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alfred was upset and burst into flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges ALFRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire that suddenly flamed up burned brightly.
